cells.tense: The read arrives whole now, and you let it arrive.
cells.act: write the order things go in
cells.ask: Put the order of something you're in the middle of on a single page — start to finish — then follow that page without revising it.
cells.core:
A read lands in you before you can say where it came from, and it usually holds. You can stand in the middle of a question without an answer yet, and things arrange themselves around you in the meantime. People get steadier near you and couldn't say why.

What's left is to give that order somewhere to live. Put the order of something you're in the middle of on a single page — start to finish — then follow that page without revising it. The shape doesn't have to be clever. The shape has to exist, so what you read has something to land in instead of passing through. Writing it out doesn't trap the read; it lets the read hold still long enough to be used.
cells.sheetLine: The read lands before you can say where it came from.
cells.verb: seeing straight to what matters before analysis gets there
cells.place: where what you are comes out as itself

cells.tense: By the time the answer matters, you will have gathered so much it can no longer be given.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Pick what you would miss most, name it to yourself plainly, and take one real step toward it this week — before you feel ready.
cells.core:
There's a way this goes wrong: the read gets buried under everything gathered to confirm it. You keep collecting, checking, comparing — not because the read is missing but because holding it would mean acting, and gathering feels like safety. The questions stop being about the thing and start feeding on themselves.

So the correction isn't more information. Choose the light to steer by and turn toward it. Pick what you would miss most, name it to yourself plainly, and take one real step toward it this week — before you feel ready. Readiness isn't coming; it wasn't standing in the way. The step is the evidence you've been trying to collect.
cells.sheetLine: You keep gathering evidence for what you already sense.

cells.tense: You stopped trusting the read a while back, and you've been asking other people to make it for you since.
cells.act: move through the fog without demanding the map
cells.ask: Take something you can't see clearly yet and move through it without asking anyone to draw you the way. Notice what you find when nobody's confirming it.
cells.core:
You used to know things before you could explain them. Somewhere along the way the read stopped arriving, or stopped being trusted when it did, and now you check it with someone else before you'll let it count — asking what they think, what they'd do, whether you're even reading it right. The opinions come back and none of them settle it.

So move through it without the drawing for a while. Take something you can't see clearly yet and move through it without asking anyone to draw you the way. Notice what you find when nobody's confirming it. What you knew wasn't gone. It was waiting for you to stop outsourcing it.
cells.sheetLine: You check your own knowing with others before yourself.

cells.tense: You've been calling your choices random, and they keep landing too well for that to be true.
cells.act: give back what is owed, and take what is yours
cells.ask: Name a recent decision you called random that worked out, say what you read that made it, and give credit where it's due — yourself included.
cells.core:
Things you decide look like guesswork from the inside, and then they turn out right often enough that guesswork stops explaining it. You read the situation before you knew you were reading it, made the call, and gave the credit to luck or instinct — as if something else had been driving. It wasn't something else.

So put it in proportion. Name a recent decision you called random that worked out, say what you read that made it, and give credit where it's due — yourself included. Not a victory lap; just the ledger set right. Naming what you saw is how the read becomes yours to keep, instead of a streak you're vaguely grateful for and slightly suspicious of.
cells.sheetLine: Luck keeps taking the credit for your read.

It survives a wrong read: even if the person simply has no problem asking, a week of not asking teaches what their own read sounds like.
